analysis:
This PR extends account erasure (T-059, TB-006).

Changed behavior:
- server_services.go:133-136: SetPrivyAuth now also wires the Privy client into s.erasure via SetPrivyUsers.
- privy_delete_user.go: new PrivyAuth.DeleteUser does DELETE auth.privy.io/api/v1/users/{PathEscape(id)} with Basic auth (appID:appSecret). 204 is success, 404 maps to ErrPrivyUserNotFound, and error strings are scrubbed of the user ID.
- keys.go:19-20 and 147-149: Keys.PrivyUserID is added. OutboxRows enqueues the privy_user target with the raw DID as external_id.
- erasure_types.go: new ErasureTargetPrivyUser.
- confirm.go:23-28: AlreadyRevokedAt marks credentials revoked before confirm, so Cancel can restore only the credentials that confirm revoked. The Cancel comment in erasure_types.go changed to match.
- rules.go adds scrub rules: api_keys.allowed_models cleared; app_attest_shadow_events deleted; app_attest_key_revocations.reason cleared; request_rejections model names and params cleared; stripe_withdrawals.failure_reason cleared; payments tx_hash rewritten and memo cleared; model_prices deleted.

Not visible in the supplied files:
- The postgres and memory store implementations of confirm, cancel and scrub.
- The outbox worker that handles the privy_user target, and where PrivyUserID is populated.
- Whether outbox rows are inserted at confirm or at scrub.
- Whether the 404 handling treats an unknown user as done.

Points for the next pass:
- Outbox delivery timing relative to the grace period and Cancel.
- The Cancel restore predicate (deleted_at == requestedAt) and the interaction with AlreadyRevokedAt.
- Clearing allowed_models to '' means all models, so it depends on keys staying revoked after the scrub.
- Rewriting payments.tx_hash could weaken any remaining tx-hash dedup, though the comment says there is no reader since #1208.
- Marker-test fixtures for the new tables and columns.

findings.detail: This PR adds a privy_user outbox target. OutboxRows() (keys.go:147-149) stores the raw Privy DID as ExternalID, even though the users rule overwrites users.privy_user_id with 'erased:<uuid>'. The DID therefore persists in erasure_outbox until the worker finishes. PrivyAuth.DeleteUser (privy_delete_user.go:21-52) then makes an irreversible, app-secret-authenticated call to auth.privy.io. The T-059 threat model and its mitigations do not cover this. Two cases need a fix or an explicit mitigation entry: (a) an outbox row delivered before the grace period ends, followed by Cancel, would leave a restored account whose Privy identity is gone and could lock the user out. (b) a wrong or stale DID would delete another person's Privy identity. Fix: add privy_user to T-059 and record in affected_files that Privy deletion is delivered only after the scrub commits. Require the worker to confirm ownership of the DID, and clear external_id once the row is delivered. Add coordinator/auth/privy_delete_user.go and outbox.go to T-059's affected files.
findings.title: Erasure threat model omits the new irreversible Privy user deletion and the outbox's retention of the Privy DID
